And even today evolution is a dominant paradigm meaning that you cannot question evolution. If you question evolution it means you're crazy. So we're going to question evolution today. Evolution says we came from monkeys, apes, and eventually the best species, Homo sapiens, won out. We are just like monkeys—monkeys who like to have sex, eat, and fart.

We're just monkeys. And this is the evolutionary tree of primates. But there are certain problems with this theory. The first problem is that if you look at evolutionary theory, you should see tremendous diversity as species develop. But why do we only have one human species? Another problem is why humans migrate all around the world. Other species of humans like to migrate too, but primates don't.

Humans like to migrate because of climate change, war, or chasing game and food. But how do you explain people going to populate Pacific islands, Micronesia? It's really dangerous to go out there for months, right? Also, how do they know there'll be islands waiting for them in the Pacific? This is very odd about humans. There are lots of things that other animals don't do.

For example, we're very religious. The Neanderthals were before Homo sapiens, but we've discovered religious ritual sites where Neanderthals engage in such practices. Religion doesn't seem to have much to do with survival. You can argue that religion is a waste of time. Why aren't they hunting? Why are they using so many resources and time on these ritual sites?

Homo sapiens did cave paintings, which are very elaborate and time-consuming. They were in deep, cold caves where there isn’t much light, yet they spent a lot of time drawing these paintings. This is not very practical. Also, when we drew on caves, we figured out how to make it artistic. We used red ochre for red and yellow pigment and charcoal for black.

We were very creative and resourceful. During the ice age, things freeze over and can be easily preserved. Most of human history was in the ice age period. The entire world was basically frozen over during that time. How did we survive? We used the resources around us. For example, they killed a mammoth and turned it into a house.

How did they know how to do this? We've been trying for a long time to figure it out. My answer is that they just knew it. Let's do a thought experiment: if you're given a wall and cannot talk or communicate with each other, drawing a picture would be disgusting and incoherent. But something weird and wonderful happens when you don't have a plan or draft.
